item.title: Iranian Turkmen FMs discuss regional developments in phone call
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and his Turkmen counterpart, Rashid Meredov, held a telephone conversation on Monday afternoon to discuss key regional issues and the latest international developments. item.title: Baqaei slams Germany European partners for contradictory stance on aggression against Iran
item.description:
Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei criticized Germany and several European countries for their contradictory positions on the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran, recalling German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s June 2025 remarks in support of Israel’s actions in a post on X and quoting German philosopher Friedrich Schiller to underscore his criticism. "June 2025: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, speaking about Israel’s aggression against Iran, said: “This is the dirty work Israel is doing for all of us.” October 2026: German Foreign Minister (and others) warn against renewed attacks on Iran and stress the need to prevent further escalation. item.title: Araghchi urges Macron to stick to his own account of Iran’s nuclear deal
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, reacting to French President Emmanuel Macron’s contradictory statements on Iran’s nuclear activities, wrote on X that Macron had pledged in 2018 that France would not withdraw from the JCPOA because it had signed the deal, but now claims to have always opposed any nuclear activity in Iran. “Stick to your own account, Mr. President!” Araghchi wrote.

item.title: Baqaei: US negotiating approach not Iranians’ religious beliefs blocks diplomacy
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei wrote on X that the US negotiating approach, characterized by unilateral demands, failure to honor commitments, and reliance on coercion, is the real obstacle to rational negotiations with Iran, not Iranians’ religious beliefs. He urged Washington to understand Iran’s strategic interests and legitimate security concerns and address its own record of breaching commitments. "What does the American administration's failure to respect its diplomatic commitments and its addiction to force and pressure have to do with the "religious beliefs" of Iranians?! Faith does not preclude 'rationality', just as secularism does not guarantee wisdom. What makes "rational negotiations" impossible is not "Iran’s religious beliefs", but America’s negotiating behavior, which amounts to little more than one-sided dictation rather than genuine diplomacy. You cannot demand concessions while refusing reciprocity, dictate terms while ignoring the other side’s legitimate interests, and expect a lasting agreement. Stop making ideologically driven assumptions about Iranians’ religious beliefs and start understanding Iran’s strategic interests and legitimate security concerns. And above all, instead of accusing others, address your own record of broken promises."

item.title: Polish Deputy Foreign Minister meets with Iranian FM Araghchi in Tehran
item.description: Wojciech Zajączkowski, Poland’s Deputy Foreign Minister, who is visiting Tehran to participate in the third round of political consultations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Poland, met with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday afternoon. Referring to the positive historical ties between the Iranian and Polish peoples, as well as the discussions held with his Polish counterpart on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, Araghchi stressed the importance of planning to make use of the existing capacities in both countries to strengthen bilateral engagement in various fields in pursuit of mutual interests. Outlining Iran’s positions on developments in West Asia, Araghchi said the insecurity in the region and the Strait of Hormuz stemmed from the aggressive actions of the United States and the Israeli regime. Criticizing the complicity or inaction of some European countries in the face of the blatant military aggression against Iran, he stressed the need for all countries, including European states, to adopt a principled position by condemning the military aggression against Iran and the crimes committed during it. The foreign minister also emphasized that, just as Iran had remained steadfast in using diplomatic tools to ensure peace and security in the region, it would not hesitate to defend its national sovereignty and territorial integrity against any threat or act of aggression. item.title: Iran’s new ambassador to Uganda meets Foreign Minister Araghchi
item.description: Reza Nourian, the newly appointed ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Uganda, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi before departing for his post and outlined his proposed plan to expand bilateral cooperation between Tehran and Kampala in various fields. The foreign minister, while wishing Nourian success in his mission in Uganda, stressed the need to make use of existing capacities and opportunities to increase trade exchanges and strengthen relations and cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly in the political, economic and agricultural sectors. Before his appointment as Iran’s new ambassador to Uganda, Nourian served as deputy director of the Department for Cultural Cooperation and NGOs at the Foreign Ministry’s Center for Public Diplomacy.

item.title: Irans new ambassador in Italy meets with FM Araghchi
item.description: Ali Akbar Rezaei, the new Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Italy, met today, Wednesday, with Seyed Abbas Araghchi, the Minister of Foreign Affairs. During this meeting, Ali Akbar Rezaei outlined his proposed plans regarding bilateral relations between Tehran and Rome. While wishing success to Iran’s new ambassador in Rome, the Iranian Foreign Minister emphasized the importance of using all opportunities to strengthen Iran’s relations with other countries. Prior to his appointment as Iran’s new ambassador to Italy, Ali Akbar Rezaei served as Director-General of the Office of Strategic Planning and Monitoring of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Iranian Russian FMs discuss bilateral ties regional developments in Tehran
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and Sergey Lavrov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation, met in Tehran on Monday, October 19, 2026, and discussed the latest state of bilateral relations and the most important regional and international developments. During the meeting, the two foreign ministers reviewed the expanding relations and cooperation between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Russian Federation and emphasized the importance of continuing regular consultations between Tehran and Moscow and following up on the implementation of bilateral agreements. The two sides also exchanged views on ways to strengthen political, economic and trade cooperation and expand interactions within the framework of the Iran-Russia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty. Regional developments, including the security situation in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, developments in Palestine and Yemen, as well as issues related to the Caucasus and Europe, were among the other topics discussed by the two foreign ministers. Araghchi and Lavrov, emphasizing the need to peacefully resolve regional disputes and crises through dialogue and political solutions, exchanged views on international developments and the need to strengthen multilateralism and cooperation in international forums. The foreign ministers of Iran and Russia also reaffirmed their countries' determination to continue close cooperation and consultation

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and Sergey Lavrov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation, met in Tehran on Monday, October 19, 2026, and discussed the latest state of bilateral relations and the most important regional and international developments. During the meeting, the two foreign ministers reviewed the expanding relations and cooperation between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Russian Federation and emphasized the importance of continuing regular consultations between Tehran and Moscow and following up on the implementation of bilateral agreements. The two sides also exchanged views on ways to strengthen political, economic and trade cooperation and expand interactions within the framework of the Iran-Russia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty. Regional developments, including the security situation in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, developments in Palestine and Yemen, as well as issues related to the Caucasus and Europe, were among the other topics discussed by the two foreign ministers. Araghchi and Lavrov, emphasizing the need to peacefully resolve regional disputes and crises through dialogue and political solutions, exchanged views on international developments and the need to strengthen multilateralism and cooperation in international forums. The foreign ministers of Iran and Russia also reaffirmed their countries' determination to continue close cooperation and consultations in order to strengthen bilateral relations and help consolidate regional and international peace, stability and security.
